thesis: The 6/4 pack contains exactly one item that speaks directly to a position I hold: 'Stocks drop on AI, rate hike worries as Lebanon deal hits oil.' I opened the XOM sleeve on 6/3 on the opposite premise (Hormuz closed, oil bid on Iran risk), and this pre-open headline contradicts that premise, so I exit the sleeve in full rather than let a thesis I no longer believe ride. The remaining energy item ('The Iran War Is Pushing the Global Gas Trade Into the Shadows') is a shadow-trade/logistics story, not a crude-price catalyst, and does not rescue the entry. On the other side of the book, the AI thread is present but is cautionary rather than fresh: dotcom-bubble-2.0 fears over trillion-dollar AI floats, 'AI Bubble or Not' commentary, the same ~$20bn Nvidia profit item I already saw on 6/3, and an AVGO earnings preview for a name I cannot trade. That is commentary, not new guidance, so I neither add to NVDA nor panic-trim it: it stays near 39% of equity, inside my 50% cap, and QQQ and XLK stay as the tech breadth sleeves. The genuinely eye-catching headlines (SpaceX IPO next week, GameStop buyback, Eli Lilly, Fluence, Credo, Gorilla/Supermicro) are all outside my tradable set or pure speculation about a private listing, and the bitcoin crash is a forbidden asset class; chasing TSLA as a SpaceX proxy would be inventing a linkage the pack does not make. Being the aggressive tier does not oblige me to spend: with no long catalyst I can actually trade, the honest move is to raise the XOM cash to roughly 22% of equity as dry powder. Sell-only, so equity is unchanged at fills: cash rises well above the 5% floor, the largest name stays under 50%, and the book holds 3 of 8 allowed positions under any plausible open print.
